bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Cash generation in H1FY27 was INR 110 Cr, a 5x+ YoY increase, computed as profit before tax less working-capital build, tax paid, lease rentals and capex, plus non-cash charges.
- Balance sheet as of Sep 30, 2026 shows cash and bank balances of INR 148 Cr (down from INR 214 Cr at FY26-end) alongside investments rising to INR 338 Cr (from INR 252 Cr), suggesting cash is being redeployed into investments rather than held idle.
- Equity base grew to INR 1,486 Cr from INR 1,412 Cr over the half year, funded internally with total liabilities rising to INR 822 Cr from INR 681 Cr, largely trade payables and other current liabilities.
- No capex, dividend or buyback plans are disclosed in the deck; PPE including CWIP remained minimal and roughly flat (INR 21 Cr vs INR 22 Cr), consistent with an asset-light, brand-led model.

business.body:
- Deck frames the long-term opportunity around a pipeline of beauty categories (hair colour, fragrance, nutraceuticals, men's skin care, oral beauty, colour cosmetics, hair care, moisturizers, face serums, face cleansers) under the theme 'Crystal-Gazing the Future of I-Beauty'.
- Hair colour is highlighted as a fast-penetrating, under-indexed category in India (<1% of BPC spend vs ~5% globally), with consumers shifting from dye to creme formats and from black to styling-led colour.
- Focus categories (Face Cleanser, Shampoo, Face Serum, Suncare, Moisturizer, Baby, Lipstick) grew 40%+ and rose to 80%+ of revenue contribution, up 369 bps YoY in Q2FY27, within a ~INR 50,000 Cr addressable market where Honasa holds ~5% share.
- Younger brands (The Derma Co, Aqualogica, Dr. Sheth's, BBlunt, Staze, BTM Ventures/Reginald Men) accelerated to 45%+ YoY growth, positioned as the next growth engine beyond the core Mamaearth brand.

deepdive.thesis: Honasa Consumer Limited is a fast-growing personal care company that has disrupted the traditional FMCG industry with its digital-first approach and is poised for further growth with its omnichannel strategy and expansion into new categories.

open.item: Company targets high single-digit growth for Mamaearth next quarter, aiming to reach double-digit growth by Q4 FY26 and maintain into next year.
Company expects to stay at least in the ~7-8% EBITDA range in the coming quarters (not raising guidance despite better H1).
Top 100 cities now fully direct; ~85% of clusters have the right distributor, with the remaining ~15% to be built over the next 3-6 months.
Company expects the serum category to keep growing ~30% next year and wants to grow faster than the category to gain share.
Core categories (75% of revenue, up from 70%) targeted to reach 84%-85% of contribution over the next 4-6 quarters.
Derma Co (INR750 crores net sales ARR, #1 sunscreen brand 2024) is building moisturizer and shampoo categories to reach INR1,000 crores+ over the next 1-2 years.
Company expects suncare to become a INR5,000 crore category by 2028 and is investing to be a strong leader.
Over the next 2-3 years Mamaearth will focus on 6 core categories; non-focus categories (next biggest: body) are declining and their contribution will keep going down.
Company plans and aspires to reach double-digit EBITDA margin by the time it hits the INR4,000 crores revenue aspiration.
Company aspires to be more than INR4,000 crores in revenue (roughly double from here) by the end of the decade.
Over the next 4-5 years, larger brands expected to reach mid-teens EBITDA range.
Mamaearth hit its goal of planting 1 million trees by 2025 and has taken a new goal to plant another 1 million trees over the next 5 years.
Company sees oral beauty as a $700 million opportunity by 2030 and intends to build Fang into a prestige oral-care leader.
Company expects color cosmetics to be a INR17,000 crore category by 2028 and more than INR20,000 crore by 2030, focusing on the lip sub-segment via Staze and Mamaearth.
Company targets to unlock 50 to 100 bps of operating margin every year, driven by procurement, mix and marketing efficiencies.
Company is watching the wellness/nutraceuticals and regimen trend and would like to take on that opportunity in the medium term, but has no crafted strategic view yet.
Company expects A&P for majority of mature brands to settle around 27%-28% of sales as they grow over the next few years.
Company has no definitive dividend policy yet; prefers to allocate cash toward growth opportunities and will deliberate on distribution in due time.
Dubai distributor case ongoing; favorable Indian High Court judgment but unfavorable first appeal in Dubai, company has filed a further appeal and remains confident of a favorable final decision.

verdicts.item: Company aims to grow at 2x to 2.5x of market growth over the next three years, translating to around a 20% CAGR.
verdicts.note: 'a 22.5% growth in revenues' (like-for-like); 'In our H1 level, we've delivered 14.5% growth' - Q2 beats 20% but H1 pace still below the 20% CAGR target. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company plans to deliver double-digit value growth in FY26.
verdicts.note: 'a 22.5% growth in revenues'; 'In our H1 level, we've delivered 14.5% growth' - company delivering double-digit value growth in FY26. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Management targets reaching double-digit EBITDA margin over the next three years, from ~7% currently.
verdicts.note: 'EBITDA continues to be stable at 8.4%'; go-forward target 'every year, we target to unlock 50 to 100 bps of operating margin' - double-digit margin still years out and annual pace lowered.

verdicts.item: Company has deployed distributors in ~70% of ward cells; remaining ~30% to be deployed over the next three to four months, with gradual recovery.
verdicts.note: 'about 85% of the clusters where we needed the right distributor and for the 15% clusters, we're still... building... over the next 3 to 6 months' - deployment progressed beyond the 70%/30% commitment…

verdicts.item: Company recognizes top 10 SKUs contribute only ~40-45% of Mamaearth (vs 75-80% for mature brands) and aims to concentrate investment on hero SKUs.
verdicts.note: 'able to build another hero SKU... rice face wash, which is our third face wash for the brand to enter the INR100 crores plus club'; core categories 75% of brand - hero-SKU concentration advancing; to…

verdicts.item: Company is building a media-mix-modelling-based strategy with internal data science and an external MMM agency to deploy a more effective media strategy next year.
verdicts.note: 'media mix modelling based learnings... the testing that we did over the 4 to 5 months and then deployed it this year, and we are clearly seeing the results of that.'

verdicts.item: Company is confident younger emerging brands can continue to grow at least 20%+, having grown 30%+ in H1.
verdicts.note: 'Young brands again continue to deliver well 20% Y-o-Y growth is what we are seeing on the young brands portfolio' - meets 20%+.

verdicts.item: Company expects to get back to FY24 (~8%) EBITDA levels within FY26, probably towards H2 FY26.
verdicts.note: 'EBITDA continues to be stable at 8.4%'; H1 'EBITDA margin of about 8%' - back to FY24 (~8%) levels, ahead of the H2FY26 timeline. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Company expects FY26 EBITDA back to FY24 levels and improvement on that base from FY27 onwards.
verdicts.note: H1 'EBITDA margin of about 8%'; Q2 8.4% - FY26 already tracking at FY24 EBITDA levels.

verdicts.item: Company appointed Tier-1 distributors in top 50 cities this quarter; full effect of transition and GT recovery expected over the next couple of quarters.
verdicts.note: 'in the top 100 cities, we have completely moved direct'; 'General trade is also on a growth trajectory in terms of secondary sales Y-o-Y' with share gains - transition/GT recovery materialized.

verdicts.item: Mamaearth pilots on product, messaging and media mix have just started; more structured learnings and a sustainable trajectory expected after Q4 and Q1.
verdicts.note: 'Mamaearth is back in green'; strategies 'deployed it this year, and we are clearly seeing the results' - sustainable trajectory emerged as expected after Q4/Q1.

verdicts.item: Company's goal is for its quick commerce market share to be higher than its e-commerce market share; QC now ~7-8% of business.
verdicts.note: 'Quick commerce is now about 10% of our revenues already and is the fastest-growing channel... relatively healthier economics' - scaled from 7-8% with healthy economics as intended.

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.
